name: Keycloak
description: Self-hosted identity provider (OIDC, OAuth2, SAML). Run one login for your other apps: create a realm, register a client, and point any OIDC-capable app at it. Production mode with a Postgres store, so realms, clients and user accounts survive a restart. Sign in at /admin/ with the generated admin password (reveal it on the install form and save it first). Harden it right after the first login, because Keycloak's defaults are permissive: in the master realm turn on Brute force detection under Realm settings, Security defenses, and turn on Login events and Admin events under Realm settings, Events. Then create a permanent admin account and delete the temporary one Keycloak bootstraps. Note that Keycloak stores SMTP settings per realm in its own database rather than in environment variables, so this greffon cannot inherit the platform SMTP integration: set mail per realm in the console, or password reset and email verification will not work. First boot runs a Quarkus build step before serving: about 20 seconds on an idle machine once the images are pulled, and several times that on a loaded one.

value.title: Admin username
value.description: Master-realm administrator, created on first boot only.

value.title: Admin password
value.description: Password for the admin console, minted by the platform. Reveal it with the eye icon and store it before you deploy. This account owns every realm on this instance, and Keycloak ships the master realm with brute-force protection OFF, so the token endpoint will accept unlimited guesses: a short human-chosen password is not safe here. Set on first boot only.

value.title: Database password
value.description: Generated by the platform at instance creation. Internal to this instance: Keycloak and Postgres share it, nothing else reads it. Do NOT regenerate it after the instance has been created. Postgres only reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD when it initialises an empty data directory, so the stored role keeps the old password while Keycloak starts with the new one and cannot connect. Changing it needs an ALTER ROLE inside the database, which the platform does not do for you.
